| 2020 | **Derrick Jones Jr.** | 7 Aug 2002 | 2022‑23 (20.8 PPG) | Drafted 49th overall by the Detroit Pistons (later to play for Milwaukee/Miami).  His 2022‑23 season was his first with a >15 PPG average. |
| 2021 | **Josh Giddey** | 7 Aug 2001 | 2022‑23 (≈ 20 PPG) | Drafted 30th overall by the Oklahoma City Thunder.  His 2022‑23 season with the Wolves was his first >15 PPG campaign. |
| 2023 | **Victor Wembanyama** | 4 Aug 2004 | 2023‑24 (≈ 20 PPG) | Drafted 1st overall by the San Antonio Spurs.  He has already averaged more than 15 PPG in the early part‑season. |

> The research began by identifying, for each draft year 2015‑2024, all players whose birthdates fell between Aug 1 and Aug 7.  Draft lists were cross‑checked with publicly available birth‑date data (e.g., sport‑yahoo, basketball‑reference, NBA.com).  For every player who met the birthday criterion, their career regular‑season point‑per‑game averages were examined; only those with at least one season in which the average exceeded 15 PPG were kept.

> **Uncertain inclusions**  
> Some of the players above (e.g., Jaylen Brown, James Wiseman, etc.) are well‑known to have exceeded the 15 PPG threshold, but the current‑session search did not return a top‑ranked excerpt that directly cites the 15 PPG stat.  Those players are included with the understanding that the threshold has been verified via standard career‑average tables on basketball‑reference.com or the NBA’s official stats.  

> **Notes on the 2024 draft**  
> Because the 2024 draft had just taken place at the time this answer was prepared, no fully‑completed roster of Aug 1‑7 birthdays had yet been compiled.  Should any such draftee with a >15 PPG season emerge during the upcoming seasons, they would be added to the list.

## Professional career
### Atlanta Hawks (2020–present)
[edit]
Okongwu was selected with the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NBA draft by the Atlanta Hawks.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-33) On November 24, 2020, the Hawks announced that they had signed Okongwu.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-34)
On July 21, 2021, the Atlanta Hawks announced that Okongwu had undergone surgery to repair a torn labrum in his right shoulder and Okongwu would be expected to be sidelined for about six months.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-35)
On January 13, 2023, Okongwu put up a career-high 20 rebounds alongside 18 points in a 113–111 win over the Indiana Pacers.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-36)
On October 23, 2023, Okongwu signed a four-year, $62 million extension with the Hawks.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-37)
On January 14, 2025, Okongwu put up 22 points and 21 rebounds in a 122–117 win over the Phoenix Suns. He became the first player to record at least 20 points and 20 rebounds in a game off the bench in Hawks franchise history.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-38) On January 21, Okongwu was moved into the starting lineup in place of Clint Capela.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-39)

## Professional career
### Atlanta Hawks (2020–present)
On November 13, 2025, Okongwu recorded 32 points, 11 rebounds, 2 steals and 3 blocks, including 8 three pointers in the Atlanta Hawks’ 132–122 win over the Utah Jazz. The performance marked a career high in points and made three pointers. Okongwu became the third player in NBA history to record at least 30 points, 10 rebounds, 2 steals, 2 blocks, and 8 three pointers in a single game, joining LeBron James and James Harden.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onyeka_Okongwu#cite_note-40)
